examples.text: I like to wear a shirt and pants. It might not be very fashionable, it might look simple, but that's the way I like it. (Thai, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2006)
I think that people watch too much TV these days and in a way this mightn't be such a good thing. (Albanian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2010)
… my parents said it might be the last holiday where we are all together. (German, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)
[talking about a lottery ticket] Lisa thought it might be a lucky one so she showed it to her Dad. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)
The park is a great place for picnic. It has lots of trees, a beautiful view and fresh air. You might need to bring some food and drink. (Turkish, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2009)
I really don't know what you should do, but I think that you might talk with your parents. (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)
[talking about an unusual sound] It might have been our neighbours' cat. (Swedish, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993)
They might have been right, but I don't agree with them. (French, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993)
He might have seen us. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)
In years past, you might have gone straight from school to your family's farm or joined your parents in the factory they worked in. (B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Polish; Pass)
Many things might have led to these changes. (B2 VANTAGE; 2007; German; Pass)
I thought that a burglar might have broken into our house. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Turkish; Pass)
As you might know, nobody came here until Wednesday afternoon. (Spanish - European, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 2010)
As you might know, I've been very busy recently taking my exams. (Danish, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1999)
As you might have noticed, I broke your beautiful vase which was in the hall. (Portuguese, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1999)
As you might have already heard, there is a delay with the setting of the new computer system. (Austria; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; German; Pass)
